validity.researcher_notes: This is a real, well-documented, single physical pipe: New Mexico Gas Company's (NMGC) 2020-2021 'Santa Fe Mainline Loop' project, a 20-inch intrastate transmission line paralleling NMGC's existing 12-inch Santa Fe Mainline along the I-25 corridor from Bernalillo to Santa Fe, NM. Confirmed independently by (1) NMGC's own May 4, 2020 press release PDF and 5-page project information packet PDF, (2) the Albuquerque Journal (Kevin Robinson-Avila, May 21 2020, read via Wayback since the live URL now 404s) quoting NMGC VP of Engineering Tom Bullard, (3) the Santa Fe New Mexican (Scott Wyland, March 2023) confirming the '20-inch-diameter pipeline, known as the Santa Fe mainline loop, was finished' in 2021, and (4) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects historical workbook, which carries a 'Santa Fe Mainline' / 'New Mexico Gas' row independently tabulating Miles=35, Diameter=20in, Cost=$60MM, Completed Date=2021-02-26 -- all matching GEM's recorded values exactly. No duplicate: no other row in the 46-row roster touches this NM route. Classification (transmission) is directly stated by the operator ('20-inch natural gas transmission pipeline') and consistent with EIA's transmission-projects-only dataset carrying the row. One internal-geometry caveat, not a value defect: the sheet's mapped RouteType/RouteAccuracy=low geometry estimates LengthEstimateKm=72.83 km vs. the independently-confirmed LengthKnownKm=56.33 km (=35 mi exactly) -- normal for a low-accuracy/schematic trace, and not evidence the recorded 56.33 km is wrong (it is the figure every independent source states). Per scope instructions this is a validity note only, no route fix proposed. Opened/verified all 7 of this row's harvested wiki citations (the archived+live nmgco infrastructure_updates pair, abqjournal, nmgco About_Us, EIA, santafenewmexican/valles-caldera, and the '5 4 20 Santa Fe Loop.pdf' press release) plus 3 more found via web search and cited in this shard: the operator's own 5-page 'SF Mainline Packet FINAL 3.pdf' (already linked in the sheet's own RouteNotes column), the direct EIA .xlsx download, and a Wayback capture of the now-404 abqjournal article.

validity.researcher_notes: The batch brief's lead was correct: Emera no longer owns New Mexico Gas Company (NMGC), the entity GEM records as both Operator and 100% Owner of this pipeline. Emera announced the sale to Bernhard Capital Partners (a Louisiana private-equity infrastructure firm) on 2024-08-05 for ~$1.25B; the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (an independent state regulator, wholly outside the transaction parties) issued final approval 2026-07-30 (prc.nm.gov docket order); Emera's own investor-relations release confirms that approval and names Bernhard Capital Partners as buyer; and NMGC's own current About Us / bcp_purchase pages state the sale closed 2026-08-12 ('New Mexico Gas Company Sale to Bernhard Capital Partners Complete... ownership of New Mexico Gas Company transferred to Bernhard Capital Partners'). Three independent origins (state regulator, seller's investor release, target company's own site) agree on the buyer name and close date -- tier=high. I did NOT stage a REFS_ADDED fill for the Owner[ref] unit citing 'Emera' -- that value is now wrong, so citing support for it would misrepresent it as current; this validity concern with `contested` is the correct surface per the batch instructions. Operator itself is unaffected: NMGC keeps its name, leadership, workforce and regulatory obligations under the new owner (all four sources above confirm this explicitly), so the Operator[ref] fill below (New Mexico Gas Company) still stands.

Found a PHMSA pipeline-safety interpretation (PI-11-0013 / PI-09-0019, ~2009-2012) that references a New Mexico 'Santa Fe transmission line' operating at 600 psig -- but both www.phmsa.dot.gov and the direct PDF path 403'd for this UA (both root and document-path attempts), AND the interpretation predates the 2020-2021 loop by 8-10 years, so on the balance of evidence it almost certainly describes the OLD 12-inch line rather than the NEW 20-inch pipe GEM tracks in this row (aggregate/wrong-segment risk -- would repeat the exact 'system figure on a segment/predecessor row' defect this sweep is watching for). Not staged for that reason as well as the access failure. No NMGC or EIA document states an operating pressure for the new line.

FuelSource wants the named upstream field/facility, not 'Natural Gas' (schema gotcha). This is an LDC looping/reinforcement project drawing on NMGC's broader distribution/transmission system (which NMGC materials describe elsewhere as fed from San Juan and Permian basin supply generally), not a line dedicated to one named field or plant. No source names a specific upstream facility for this segment; leaving blank rather than guessing.

The Albuquerque Journal (May 2020) reports the project was part of ~$400M in NMGC infrastructure investment (Sept 2017-YE2021) for which NMGC filed a rate case at the NM PRC in December 2019 to recover costs -- but that rate case covers MULTIPLE capital projects together, and I could not find a document that gives a Santa Fe-Mainline-specific proposal/announcement date distinct from the May 2020 construction-start date already on the sheet. Leaving ProposalYear/Month unresolved rather than reusing the Dec-2019 rate-case date, which would misattribute a multi-project filing date as this project's own proposal date.
